A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the GePBench study. Their text, figures, tables, algorithms, and Appendices A–F support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original model and human evaluations, visual-encoder and noise analyses, and downstream experiments with LLaVA-GeP.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, downstream training experiments, error analyses, module-specific fine-tuning, probing, and evaluations on hand-drawn and real-world diagrams.

M1.justification: The synthesis pipeline and two-stage GeP training remain. Algorithm 1 changes fixed-attempt sampling and overlap-threshold filtering to validity-rule rejection sampling with an explicit shape-count stopping condition. Appendix C also adds a Qwen3-based model implementation using Qwen3-VL vision features, a newly initialized projector, and Qwen3-8B.

E1.justification: v3 expands the reported shape/relationship pools from 10/9 to 15/11 and adds medical, document, We-Math, hand-drawn, and real scientific diagram evaluations. The human population also broadens. MATH-Vision, ChartQA, and LLaVA-Wild transfer evaluations disappear; MathVista remains in the human-gap comparison but leaves the transfer evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands from 20 to 32 model configurations, adding GPT-5.2, Gemini-2.5-Pro, newer Qwen and InternVL families, G-LLaVA, Math-LLaVA, Math-PUMA, and QVQ-Preview. Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-1.5-Pro, and InternVL2.5-26B are removed. Transfer comparisons add a Qwen3-based baseline, and comparator membership also changes in the noise and shape-count analyses.

E3.justification: Human evaluation changes from five undergraduates to 25 adults aged 20–50, with revised question sampling whose allocation is less explicit in v3. New protocols include 10K-example module-specific fine-tuning and 1.6K/0.4K training/test samples per probing task. The GPT-4o checkpoint changes from August to November 2024; the principal zero-shot, temperature-zero, 640×640 evaluation settings remain.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix D add a 200-case GPT-4o error analysis, InternVL token-probability and saliency analyses, module-specific fine-tuning, and linear probes investigating failure sources. Appendix E adds hand-drawn and real-world robustness tests. Existing encoder, shape-count, and synthetic-noise analyses are retained and updated, with more detailed noise results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new diagnostic probability and frequency tables report point estimates rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Many scores in Tables 1–2 and the downstream figures change. LLaVA-1.5-7B's GePBench average changes from 39.2 to 37.1; ChartBench baseline/GeP scores change from 10.3/14.8 to 45.3/46.4. Numerous model, diagnostic, and natural-diagram results are added. Revised construction and checkpoints, plus incompletely explained score revisions, limit direct same-setting performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical results, proofs, or formal derivations. The added numerical shape constraints and probing thresholds specify construction and evaluation procedures, without introducing theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims about the benchmark, deficient geometric perception, and downstream benefits remain. The introduction adds an explicit cross-architecture generalization claim involving Qwen3 and extends the stated downstream benefits to medical and document applications.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations involving systematic response biases, shape miscomprehension, and the LLM backbone as a principal failure source. It explains possible noise benefits through boundary and texture cues and discusses why specialized reasoning models underperform. The earlier limited-scaling interpretation is removed, while existing encoder-invariance explanations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds detailed geometric validity constraints, question-generation limits, and distractor construction rules. Other additions document Qwen3 initialization, diagnostic procedures, model sources, and medical evaluation subsets. v3 reports code and data availability with a repository link, replacing v2's future-release promise. Existing LLaVA optimizer, hardware, and training-budget disclosures largely remain.

R1.justification: Literature coverage expands across spatial cognition, computational geometry, newer model families, specialized geometric/reasoning models, and medical/document benchmarks. The discussion adds an explicit connection to QVQ's reported recognition limitations. The original positioning against reasoning-focused geometry benchmarks remains; publication and bibliographic updates to retained works do not constitute additions.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory motivation are substantially rewritten, and benchmark construction receives expanded explanations. Earlier experimental subsections are reorganized into a Discussion section and appendices; encoder discussion moves into the main text, while shape-count and human-gap discussions move out. Appendix organization changes substantially, and the standalone Limitations section is removed.

P2.justification: v3 redraws and rearranges examples, expands the downstream radar charts to four model series and revised benchmark axes, and adds error-distribution, example, and saliency displays. New diagnostic and robustness tables substantially expand the visual presentation. Existing plots are relocated or redrawn, the noise bar chart becomes detailed tables, and the document adopts a different conference layout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens generalization evidence through matched Qwen3-based training comparisons and direct hand-drawn and real scientific diagram tests, extending v2's single-architecture transfer and synthetic-noise analyses. Detailed construction rules and new diagnostics also improve reproducibility and explanatory depth. Unexplained score revisions and ambiguities such as relation probing described with single-shape images limit some interpretations, but the new generalization tests and construction documentation provide a substantial net quality gain.
